ext.autostart.note: Auto-start runs this whenever Chrome opens.
ext.error.denied.body: On a work or school computer this is usually a policy your IT team sets, and AwakeTab can't get around it. The web tool asks the browser a different way and may still work.
ext.error.nothing: Nothing is keeping this device awake.
ext.error.unsupported.body: Open AwakeTab in a tab instead. The tab keeps the screen awake while it stays visible.
ext.error.unsupported.meta: No power API in this browser.
ext.error.unsupported.title: This browser doesn't give extensions the power API.
ext.extend.note: The screen can sleep again now. Add time to keep it awake. Offered until {time}.
ext.footer.honest: No ads on the awake screen, now or later.
ext.options.duration.help: Used when you click Start in the popup or press the shortcut.
ext.options.end.askHelp: The popup offers +15 min, +30 min or +1 h for five minutes.
ext.options.end.stopHelp: The session ends quietly at its end time.
ext.options.lead: Settings save here and sync through your Chrome account; your licence never syncs. Pro sections are marked.
ext.options.locale.help: The popup, these settings and notifications.
ext.options.lockedMore: The controls below stay readable but locked.
ext.options.navNote: Changes save as you make them and apply to the popup right away.
ext.options.shortcut.label: Toggle from any tab:
ext.options.shortcuts.help: In the popup: Space starts or stops, 1 to 6 pick a length, 0 means no limit, U sets an end time.
ext.options.theme.auto: Follows your system and switches with it.
ext.popup.noEnd: No end time. Stop when you are done.
ext.private.body: You allowed AwakeTab in Incognito. This is the same session as your other windows, so Stop here stops it everywhere. AwakeTab can't see the pages you open.
ext.private.title: Private window
ext.pro.body: Run on a weekly plan, like weekdays 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, or start when Chrome opens. Everything else here stays free.
ext.schedule.levelHelp: This schedule sets the level. A change here applies to sessions you start yourself.
ext.schedule.levelSaved: Saved for sessions you start yourself. This schedule keeps its own level.
ext.schedule.skips: Skips the rest of this window. It starts again {when}.
ext.tips.pin: Pin it to see time left.
ext.tips.shortcut: starts or stops from any tab.
ext.tips.title: Good to know
ext.update.aria: What's new in version {version}, opens the changelog
ext.welcome.cant.closed: It works only while Chrome is running. With Chrome closed, nothing keeps the device awake.
ext.welcome.cant.lid: It can't stop sleep when you close the lid. It works while Chrome is running, even with the tab hidden or the window minimised.
ext.welcome.cant.presence: It doesn't keep you "Available" in Teams, Slack or Zoom. Those follow your typing, and AwakeTab never fakes input.
ext.welcome.cant.title: What it can't do
ext.welcome.figure: Chrome toolbar showing where to pin AwakeTab
ext.welcome.how.title: What happens when you use it
ext.welcome.how1.body: Click the icon and choose a length, or an end time like {time}. Start uses your default length.
ext.welcome.how1.title: Pick how long
ext.welcome.how2.body: Switch tabs, hide the window, minimise Chrome. The badge counts down, and it only appears while the device is really being kept awake.
ext.welcome.how2.title: It holds while you work
ext.welcome.how3.body: Turn on notifications in Settings and Chrome shows one when the session ends, with +30 min and Stop. The popup also offers more time for five minutes.
ext.welcome.how3.title: It tells you when time is up
ext.welcome.key.body: It uses your default length. On a Mac, Alt is the Option key.
ext.welcome.key.title: {shortcut} starts or stops from any tab
ext.welcome.lead: It keeps your screen, or your whole computer, awake for as long as you choose, and it says plainly whether that is working. Pinned, its icon shows the time left at a glance.
ext.welcome.level.lead: The popup has one switch for how awake to keep things. Screen is the default. You can change it any time, even mid-session.
ext.welcome.level.screenGood: For reading, recipes, dashboards and slides: anything you watch.
ext.welcome.level.systemGood: For downloads, uploads, builds and long exports: anything that runs on its own.
ext.welcome.level.title: Screen or System
ext.welcome.next.body: Level, default length, notifications and language live in Settings. AwakeTab itself lives in your toolbar.
ext.welcome.next.title: Set your defaults, then close this tab
ext.welcome.pinCaption: Try it here: click the pin. In Chrome, the icon then stays next to the address bar.
ext.welcome.pinnedCaption: Pinned. The icon stays in view, and its badge shows the minutes left while a session runs.
ext.welcome.see.account: No account, no ads, and nothing to sign in to.
ext.welcome.see.data: Anonymous usage data is off unless you turn it on, and never includes URLs, tab titles or site names.
ext.welcome.see.permissions: It asks for power, storage and alarms. Notifications only if you turn them on; site access only for auto-start sites you add, one at a time.
ext.welcome.see.title: What it can see
ext.welcome.step1: Click the puzzle piece at the right of Chrome's toolbar.
ext.welcome.title: AwakeTab is ready. Pin it where you can see it.
